newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bangkok Governor Bhichit Rattakul has announced a flood alert as more monsoon rains have been forecast and a flood surge from the provinces is expected to reach the capital next week.

- Key opposition members will meet today to map out a common strategy in an apparent move to block the New Aspiration Party (NAP) from emerging as the biggest political party after next month's general election. They have criticised cheque-book politics and lashed out at the NAP for accepting politicians from other parties without considering their qualifications.

- PollWatch, the election watchdog, will again be entrusted with the responsibility to monitor the activities of candidates to ensure they don't violate the law during the run-up to the November 17 polls. (BANGKOK POST)
- The Board of Investment has proposed the creation of a special investment zone covering 12 northeastern provinces in which more generous incentives will be offered to attract

- The state-run National Housing Authority has found that only five percent out of the total of 300,000 housing units in Bangkok and its neighbouring provinces have been sold out. The Authority expects that the situation may improve next year when people from other provinces migrate to the capital. (MANAGER)

- Hemaraj Land and Development has emerged the big winner after General Motors picked Hemaraj's Industrial Estate on the Eastern Seaboard in Rayong province for its $750-million automobile assemply plant. (BUSINESS DAY)
